# Architecture Decision Records

ADRs preserve the **why** behind load-bearing decisions — the kind that survive rewrites and need to make sense to a reader months later. Other docs describe the *what*; ADRs describe the *why we chose this what*.

Why this file earns its place here: a comparison whose reasoning was never written down — why one embedding model beat another, say — has to be reconstructed from memory months later, and reconstruction is always worse than a record. And the thesis has to be written in November — a record written at the moment of the decision is the material that write-up draws on. A decision made and not recorded gets reconstructed later, badly.

An ADR records a decision **that was made**. It is never a proposal and never a plan. Research direction belongs to Jahid and his supervisor: an agent writes down a decision *they* took, never one it took on their behalf.

When to write a new one:

- A non-obvious choice with viable alternatives that someone might later question or try to reverse.
- A decision that constrains future work — a rule a later session has to keep obeying.
- Decisions of this shape earn a record: when the dataset changes, when the evaluation method changes, when the way few-shot examples are selected changes, when one model family or embedding model is chosen over another, when the evaluation set is split differently. These are examples of the *shape* of a decision, not a list of things to go decide.

**Separate the human's decision from the implementer's defaults, and label arbitrary choices as arbitrary.** When a record has to carry both — Jahid decided *that* something exists, an agent decided *how* it works — keep them in different sections, say plainly which is which, and where a default had no evidence behind it, write "this is arbitrary" instead of retrofitting a rationale. A plausible-sounding reason invented after the fact is the worst outcome, because it survives review and gets cited in November as if it had been reasoned. ADR [0019](./0019-musique-answering-backend-conventions.md) put the implementer's part under its own heading; ADR [0021](./0021-clustering-pool-construction-strategy.md) additionally names which of its defaults are arbitrary. *(Convention captured from the PR #34 review, 2026-08-20; first instance ADR 0021.)*

When **not** to write one:

- Conventions that are obvious from the code (naming, folder layout) — a short note beside the code is enough.
- One-off implementation details with no reach beyond the file they live in.
- Version bumps with no semantic impact.

## Template

```markdown
# NNNN. <Short title in title case>

- **Status**: Accepted | Superseded by [NNNN](./NNNN-...) | Deprecated
- **Date**: YYYY-MM-DD (or "captured retroactively YYYY-MM-DD" for past decisions)

## Context

What forces are at play? What problem are we solving? What constraints exist (time, compute, data)? Cite the specific result or pain point that drove the decision if there was one.

## Decision

The rule adopted, stated as a positive directive ("We do X"). Be precise enough that a reader can apply the rule in a new situation.

## Consequences

What changes because of this decision? What's now easier? What's now harder? What follow-up work or future risk does this create?

## Alternatives considered

Other options on the table and why they lost. This is what stops the next person from re-litigating the same debate.
```

Numbering is **gap-free**, starting at `0001`. If a record is superseded, **leave it in place** and mark its status — never renumber, and never reuse a number. A number is claimed before it is cited by an index row with status `Reserved (<who>, <date>) — <one line>` and no link — never a stub file; an abandoned reservation keeps its row, marked `abandoned (number never reused)` (ADR [0040](./0040-harness-conventions-opus-only-agents-and-id-reservation.md) item 2).

**Amendments are marked on both ends.** An ADR that changes an earlier one carries an `Amends [NNNN]` line under its status, **and** the earlier ADR gets a dated in-place note pointing forward — at the changed clause, or under the status block when the amendment touches the record as a whole — never a silent rewrite, and never an unmarked contradiction. (Convention made explicit 2026-08-20; earlier ADRs follow it in varying shapes.)

Filenames are `NNNN-kebab-case-title.md`, and every new record is added to the index table above in the same commit.
